title: Is there any gpu memory difference when using different context in TensorRT 8.4.0.6 ?
body: Hi, I have a further question about difference between `createExecutionContext` and `createExecutionContextWithoutDeviceMemory`,  Is there have any gpu memory difference when using the corresponding context ?

comments.author: lix19937
comments.body:
An engine @ deserialization, allocates device memory to store the model weights.   
Since the serialized engine is almost all weights, its size is a good approximation to the amount of device memory the weights require.

An ExecutionContext uses 2 kinds of device memory:     
+ Persistent memory required by some layer implementations - for example, some convolution implementations use edge masks, and this state cannot be shared between contexts as weights are, because its size depends on the layer input shape, which may vary across contexts. This memory is allocated on creation of the execution context, and lasts for its lifetime.

+ Scratch memory, used to hold intermediate results while processing the network. This memory is used for intermediate activation tensors. It is also used for temporary storage required by layer implementations, the bound for which is controlled by `setMaxWorkspaceSize()`.

You may optionally create an execution context without scratch memory using `createExecutionContextWithoutDeviceMemory()` and provide that memory yourself for the duration of network execution. This allows you to share it between multiple contexts that are not running concurrently, or for other uses while inference is not running.

comments.author: Jsy0220
comments.body:
@lix19937 ok, thank you for your answer. 
One more question: 
Is the total memory (Persistent + Scratch) the same no matter what execution context used (`createExecutionContextWithoutDeviceMemory` or `createExecutionContext`)？
Thanks !!

comments.author: lix19937
comments.body:
> Is the total memory (Persistent + Scratch) the same no matter what execution context used (createExecutionContextWithoutDeviceMemory or createExecutionContext)？

Yes when you only use one ctx.

comments.author: Jsy0220
comments.body: okay, what if use more than one ctx ?

comments.author: lix19937
comments.body:
For createExecutionContextWithoutDeviceMemory in multi-ctxs    
Persistent memorys in each ctx + the share memory between multiple contexts = total memory

comments.body: @lix19937  okay, i see. Thank you !!

comments.author: HuangYison
comments.body: I have a question. If I want to manually allocate scratch memory for each context, how do I calculate the minimum size I need to apply for? @lix19937

comments.author: HuangYison
comments.body:
I am using multithreading for parallel inference, but the inference time is still long. I consulted the documentation and found that the default memory application strategy for creating a context is KSTATIC, which will apply for the maximum size in all configuration files. Observing the running output, I found that when I set the batch of maxShapes to 128, 4150M of device memory will be allocated. If I create multiple threads, it will quickly exhaust the GPU's dedicated memory and then apply for shared memory. I think it is because the calculation on shared memory makes the entire inference very slow, so I want to know if I can calculate the actual memory size required?
My test environment is: GPU 4090 24G, 
TensorRT version 10.1
model: yolov8-seg, shape is 3x640x640
Thanks.

getDeviceMemorySizeForProfileV2: Return the device memory size required for a certain profile.

So, you can check it.

I probably create 10-15 threads at the same time when test, and according to one thread and one context, it does use 4*num of context, which is about 50-60G of memory.

comments.author: lix19937
comments.body: You can disable the tactics of `CUBLAS, CUBLAS_LT, CUDNN` to decrease the mem use.  Another way, if use the share device ctx, you add mutex.

I'm not actually sure how to do that. Can you give a more detailed step-by-step or is there a section of the official documentation that include this part? Thank you.

comments.author: HuangYison
comments.body:
Use trtexec command line and c++ api，the trtexec command is 
```
trtexec --onnx=v1-n-seg-dynamic.onnx --saveEngine=v1-n-seg-1-128-128.engine --memPoolSize=workspace:24G --tacticSources=-CUBLAS,-CUBLAS_LT,-CUDNN --minShapes=images:1x3x640x640 --optShapes=images:128x3x640x640 --maxShapes=images:128x3x640x640 --fp16 --verbose
```
C++ API is the same, just add the code snippet you posted to disable the tactis.

I think it is because tensorrt10.1 already disabled by default? I posted it above.
